title: FaceRecord
description: One detected face in one frame: where it is, what it looks like as an embedding, which cluster it fell into, and -- separately and much more cautiously -- which person we are willing to say it is.
$comment: PRECISION OVER RECALL (CLAUDE.md hard rule 5). A wrong person in a family album is a catastrophic failure, so identity is deliberately split into three independent things: `cluster` (unsupervised, cheap, may be wrong), `identity.person_id` (a claim), and `identity.eligible_for_automated_output` (permission to act on the claim). Only the third gates unattended output, and it is false unless a human confirmed the assignment or the model cleared the high-confidence threshold. Everything uncertain goes to the review queue rather than into an album.

face_id.description: BLAKE3 over (media_id, frame_time, quantised bbox, detector model_id+version). Content-addressed, so re-running the same detector on the same frame produces the same id and re-detection is idempotent. Changing detector version deliberately produces new ids rather than silently mutating old ones.

media_id.description: The MediaRecord this face was found in. For spanned video this is the assembly record, so a face track can cross a chapter boundary.

frame_time.description: Position within the video, in SOURCE time (already mapped back through the proxy frame index). Null for stills.

track.description: Face track membership for video. One person walking through a 4-second shot is ~120 FaceRecords sharing a track_id; the ranking and moment layers work on tracks, not frames.

embedding.description: Recognition embedding. Null when the face was detected but was too small, too blurred or too occluded to embed reliably -- an unembeddable face is still worth recording, because it counts toward 'how many people are in this photo'.

bbox.description: Normalised against the ORIENTED frame, so the same box is valid on the 512px thumbnail the detector saw and on the 6000px original the renderer will crop.

detected_on.description: Which rendition the detector ran against. Small faces missed on a thumbnail are re-detected at full resolution on demand; recording this makes 'have we already looked properly' answerable.

face_area_ratio.description: Fraction of the frame the box covers. The single best predictor of whether an embedding will be trustworthy, and a hard input to the automated-output threshold.

scheme.description: Point count and ordering convention. Consumers must switch on this rather than assuming an index layout.

FaceAttributes.title: FaceAttributes
FaceAttributes.description: Everything that decides whether this is a GOOD photo of this person, as opposed to whether it is this person. Feeds face-quality scoring, album hero selection, and the 'is anyone blinking' check.

yaw_deg.description: Head pose. Beyond about +/-45 degrees yaw, recognition confidence degrades sharply and the automated-output threshold should tighten.

eyes_open.description: Probability both eyes are open. The blink check that saves an album spread.

occlusion.description: How much of the face is hidden by a hand, hair, mask or another person.

quality.description: Fused face quality, the value album selection actually sorts on.

ClusterMembership.title: ClusterMembership
ClusterMembership.description: Unsupervised grouping over embedding distance (HDBSCAN over cosine). A cluster is a hypothesis, not an identity: it is allowed to be wrong, which is exactly why it is stored separately from `identity`.

membership_strength.description: HDBSCAN membership probability. Low values sit near the decision boundary and are precisely the ones the active-learning loop should ask a human about first -- ten well-chosen taps fix a thousand photos.

is_noise.description: HDBSCAN noise point: too far from any cluster. Never surfaces in automated output.

clustering_run_id.description: Which clustering pass produced this. Re-clustering a growing library reshuffles cluster ids; pinning the run makes the reshuffle auditable instead of mysterious.

Identity.title: Identity
Identity.description: Who we say this is, how sure we are, and whether that is sure enough to act on unattended.

person_id.description: Null until an assignment exists. A person is a user-facing entity created by labeling, never by clustering alone.

assignment.description: How the person_id was arrived at. `auto_below_threshold` is a real, common state: the model has a guess it is not allowed to use, which is the entire point of precision-first.

confidence.description: Calibrated similarity-to-person confidence. Null when unassigned.

threshold_profile.description: Which operating point was applied. `automated_output` is the strict one tuned for >=99% precision (build plan section 7); `search_only` is permissive because a wrong hit in a search result is a shrug, not a catastrophe.

threshold_used.description: The actual numeric threshold applied, stored so that retuning the operating point is a replayable decision rather than a silent behaviour change.

eligible_for_automated_output.description: THE GATE. Album, film and reel selection may only treat this face as a known person when this is true. Invariant, enforced in tests: true requires assignment to be user_confirmed, or auto_high_confidence with confidence >= threshold_used. Every other state is false.

candidates.description: Runner-up people considered. Populated when assignment is ambiguous_multiple_candidates, which is the twins-and-siblings case that a single best-match number hides.

allOf.$comment: Machine-checked half of the precision invariant: the two assignment states that can never be eligible. The positive direction (eligible implies confidence >= threshold) is asserted in the golden tests, since JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling values.
An eligible face must name a person and must state the confidence and threshold that justified it. No unexplained permissions.

SensitiveFlags.title: SensitiveFlags
SensitiveFlags.description: Child-face labeling sits behind separate explicit consent (build plan section 8). Modelled here rather than on the person so that the gate is evaluated at the point of use.

minor_status.description: `unknown` is the default and is NOT treated as adult. Estimated age is a signal for asking the user, never a licence to proceed.

labeling_consent.description: Required before a confirmed_minor face may be labeled with a person identity. Absent consent, the face is still detected and counted, but never named.

is_track_representative.description: The single best frame of this track, chosen by face quality. Identity is decided once per track from the representative, not voted per frame -- 120 correlated votes are not 120 pieces of evidence.
